newsitem.title: GERMANY: Steady cocoa buying seen in Germany, volumes thin.
newsitem.headline: Steady cocoa buying seen in Germany, volumes thin.

text.p: German cocoa bean processors are buying replacement cover to feed relatively active plants, undeterred by sterling's highs against the mark, traders said on Wednesday.
Traders reported some trades of afloat and local stock material which they said showed consumer cover was low.
But physical markets were well supplied and fundamentals looked positive so trade volumes remained limited.
Traders said consumers were expecting price falls on the futures markets after the exodus of funds and other investors.
"I can't see any upward momentum in futures, the crops are looking too good and whenever we pass on an industry order we are offered beans at a discount to futures," one trader said.
He saw London futures stuck in a broad 1,000-1,050 stg range on September.

The chocolate industry was in a more confident mood than in recent weeks after a higher than expected cocoa grind result in the second quarter of 1997, published on Monday, pointed to reasonable chocolate sales, traders also noted.
Second half 1997 beans of good West African quality were at 3.05-3.06 marks/kg cif in local import markets.
First half 1998 cif beans of good West African quality were at 3.16 marks/kg.
The cocoa butter ratio over futures remained unchanged at 2.39 for third quarter and 2.46 for fourth quarter delivery.
Butter prices liquid, ex-works, were at 7.70 marks for 1997 and first quarter 1998 was at 7.80.
Sterling was at 2.9670 marks at the Frankfurt exchange fixing on Wednesday.
